first_impression.reaction: Okay, this is exactly what I typed in. The first paragraph tells me what it is, the download link is right there, and no sign-up. I tapped it before I even got to the takeaways. Then I scrolled down to see what the columns are, because I want to know if I have to delete half of them.

journey.quote: Ours downloads as an Excel file with no sign-up, opens in Google Sheets as well, and carries the travel columns a destination wedding needs: flights, arrival and departure, accommodation and visa letters.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first two sentences. No email wall. That alone makes me trust the page.
Download above the fold on my phone. That's what I came for.

journey.quote: Give every guest their own row and tie the people who share an invitation together with one Household ID.
journey.reaction: Useful. I didn't know whether to do it by person or by family, and this settles it in one line.

journey.section: Download the wedding guest list template
journey.quote: Row 6 of the Guest list tab is an example. Overwrite it or delete it, then start your own guests at row 7. Pale yellow cells are the ones you fill in.
journey.reaction: Clear, practical. I know exactly where to start typing.

journey.quote: In Google Sheets, open a spreadsheet, choose File, then Import, select the file and choose Create new spreadsheet.
journey.reaction: Fine on a laptop, but I'm on the train on my phone. I'm not sure this works from the Sheets app, so I'll probably do it later at home.

journey.quote: Each cell takes Not invited, Invited, Attending or Declined.
The four event columns offer the five reply options.
journey.reaction: Wait, five? Earlier it listed four. Now I'm wondering if I've missed one or the article is wrong. Small thing, but it makes me double check everything else.

journey.quote: Save the date sent, Invitation sent, Arrival date and Departure date accept dates only. Type them as day/month/year.
journey.reaction: Good that it says which format. I use day/month/year anyway, but my Google account might be set to US, and the page doesn't say what happens then.

journey.quote: Read across these eight columns and a destination wedding starts to look like a logistics project. A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: Here's the sales bit. It's short and it comes after the useful stuff, so I don't mind, but I just skip it. I'm not having a destination wedding.

journey.quote: This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Dated, so I know it's current. Not why I came, but the tip about a separate file for my mum chasing her side is actually handy.

journey.quote: One row per person, grouped by a Household ID. You count meals, seats and flights by person, and invitations and envelopes by household. The template does both.
journey.reaction: FAQ answers are short and direct. This is the kind of page I'd bookmark.

unanswered_questions: Can I open or import this on my phone in the Google Sheets app, or do I need a computer?
Is there a Google Sheets copy I can just make a copy of, instead of downloading and importing an Excel file?
What happens to the date columns if my Google Sheets or Excel is set to a month/day/year region?
Is the event reply dropdown four options or five? The page says both.

turn_offs_found.quote: The four event columns offer the five reply options.
turn_offs_found.why: Contradicts the four options listed under Events and the four shown in the Summary table. Makes me doubt the details.

would_share_with: My fiance, so we can both fill it in
My mum, for the bit about sharing a cut-down copy

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, start with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-guest-list-template&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I came for a spreadsheet, and I got it. The planning service is for a destination wedding I'm not having. The pitch didn't annoy me because the template came first, but nothing here would make me enquire today. I might look at the planning app link later once RSVPs start.

top_3_changes: Fix the reply-option count in Dropdowns so it matches the four options listed under Events (exact edit in suggested_edits).
Say whether the Google Sheets import works from a phone, or that it needs a computer, since many readers arrive on mobile (needs confirming by the team, not guessed).
Add one line on what to do if the spreadsheet's region uses month/day/year dates (needs confirming by the team, not guessed).

suggested_edits.old: The four event columns offer the five reply options.
suggested_edits.new: The four event columns offer Not invited, Invited, Attending or Declined.
suggested_edits.why: Matches the four options already stated under Events and in the Summary tab description. Removes a contradiction. Adds no new facts. If the file genuinely has a fifth option, the Events section needs updating instead.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a mobile search visitor who doesn't know the brand
No invented brand facts; gaps listed in unanswered_questions

Suggested edit is an exact old/new string and adds no prices, statistics, 'free', vendor names, fees, on-the-ground claims, room blocks, availability, or implication that the Advisor manages the guest list or visas
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments ignored as invisible

open_questions.question: Does the dropdown in the event columns have four options (Not invited, Invited, Attending, Declined) or five? The Events and Dropdowns sections disagree.
Can the .xlsx be imported via the Google Sheets mobile app, and is a Google Sheets 'make a copy' version planned? Readers on phones will ask.

assumptions: Priya is planning a non-destination wedding and arrived via a Google search for 'wedding guest list template' on her phone.
Image slots render as described and don't slow the page noticeably.
